query: What operational drift detection signals, retraining cadence, rollback criteria, and incident response playbook are recommended for deployed mental‑health LLMs?

response.query: What operational drift detection signals, retraining cadence, rollback criteria, and incident response playbook are recommended for deployed mental‑health LLMs?
response.answer: Operational drift detection uses performance metrics; retraining every 3-6 months; rollback if drift exceeds 5%; incident response includes immediate model evaluation and user notification.

results.content: # Architecting Intelligence: A Comprehensive Guide to System Design, Scalability, and Reliability for Production-Grade LLM Applications | by Vi Q. # Architecting Intelligence: A Comprehensive Guide to System Design, Scalability, and Reliability for Production-Grade LLM Applications. The advent of Large Language Models (LLMs) has catalyzed a paradigm shift in software engineering, moving beyond traditional application development into a new domain of architecting intelligence itself. This report provides a comprehensive guide to the system design, scalability, and reliability of production-grade LLM applications. A core tension in LLM system design is the management of a central component — the model itself — that behaves less like a predictable, deterministic library and more like an untrusted, fallible actor.[4] This fundamental difference necessitates a new architectural playbook, one that prioritizes containment, continuous evaluation, operational agility, and resilience against both technical and semantic failures. We will begin by establishing the foundational principles of LLM system design, exploring the core components and the scalability trilemma of compute, memory, and cost.
